 53

 COMPENSATION

Off-Duty Pay

As always, the City of Cabot strives to be compliant with all Federal and State employment
laws, especially anything in relation to wage and hour laws.

The City is aware that for all uniformed personnel, including Dispatch, sometimes the job
necessitates outside of scheduled work hours to check emails, receive phone calls, etc. To
be in compliance with the above-said laws, the City wants to make sure that even though
these instances are brief, sometimes not even a full minute, these instances are
compensated. The City understands it would be burdensome on the employee and the
City to report and track how often an employee checks an email or receives one and two-
minute calls.

Therefore, each uniformed employee will receive half an hour added to each bi-weekly
pay period. This half an hour will be coded and referred to as Off-Duty Pay. Off-duty pay
will be counted as hours worked for the purposes of determining overtime.

The City believes that an extra half an hour per pay period is more than sufficient to cover
any emails checked or phone calls received. If for any reason a uniformed employee
believes he or she is working off the clock more than half an hour in a two-week period, it
is the employee’s responsibility to document and report this to the supervisor to be
sufficiently paid. Please note, that if the employee’s job requires an employee to be on-
call, the employee will still receive the additional half an hour of Off-Duty Pay.

If any uniformed personnel are on Workers’ Compensation, FMLA, Catastrophic Leave,
or LWOP, the employee will NOT receive this extra pay, as it will be presumed that
employees taking such leave are not performing work for the City. If the employee does
in fact perform work for the City during such a period of absence, the employee must
document and report this to the supervisor to be sufficiently paid. Any such work must
either be preapproved by the employee’s supervisor or must be unavoidable given the
nature of the employee’s job.

On-Call Pay

The City may require employees to be available outside of normal scheduled working
hours as a part of the essential duties of their job. In these instances, employees will be
compensated with “on-call” pay. This pay will be a flat rate and will be added to timecards
by the supervisor. If an employee has on-call pay during a pay period in which an
employee is eligible for overtime, then the on-call pay will be configured into the regular
rate of pay, and the employee be paid accordingly.

Employees do not have to be paid for “on-call” unless their activities are overly restricted.
For questions regarding this, please reach out to your supervisor or the Human Resources
Department.

 55

 COMPENSATION

Training

The City is committed to continuing training for all employees. The Mayor or Department
Head may assign City personnel to attend various training courses, seminars, and
workshops. If the employee feels that additional training is needed, he/she should notify
his/her Department Head. The training must be necessary and job-related. If approved,
the training must fit within budget constraints.

These training activities are to be considered as part of the normal work of the City rather
than leave. The City will pay the cost of the courses it requires. Expenses incurred with
on-the-job training will be paid by the City.

Training that keeps an employee away from home overnight is travel away from home.
Travel away from home is clearly work time when it cuts across the employee's workday.
This also includes travel during corresponding hours on nonworking days.

Fire Department Training

In the rare circumstances Fire Department personnel attending training will cause a
reduction in scheduled hours, the Fire Chief may approve what will be labeled as
“Training” time. These training hours will be in the employee’s PTO bank along with other
paid time off options.

On January 1st of each year, each Firefighter except for the Fire Chief will be given this
“Training” time up to 120 hours. This PTO option will never exceed 120 hours in a
calendar year, will not be paid out upon separation, cannot be used for anything other
than a shortage of hours due to training, and will count towards overtime.

For example, if a Firefighter attending an 80-hour class over a two-week span is scheduled
to work 96 hours, that Firefighter may be approved for 16 hours out of this Training PTO
option. In that same example, if a Firefighter adds a regular shift on the weekend and now
has 104 hours of worked time, that Firefighter cannot request those same 16 hours.

Once again, this time MUST be approved by the Fire Chief. For more information on
Travel, please refer to the section titled Travel.

 56

 COMPENSATION

Travel

The City will reimburse employees per diem and mileage allowances up to the IRS
allowable reimbursement rate in effect at the time of travel. Using this method,
reimbursements are excluded from the employee’s gross income and are not reported on
Form W-2.

Prior to any travel by a City employee, the Department Head must submit to Human
Resources a Request for Travel (CCT-1) form. All known and estimated costs associated
with the travel will be annotated on the CCT-1. If approved, this form will be used to pay
any advanced registration fees and/or lodging, if applicable. The Mayor and Human
Resources will verify and authorize all travel including making changes such as correct
rates or using a rental car instead of a personal vehicle.

Upon return, employees are required to submit a Travel Reimbursement Form (CCT-2)
for reimbursement. Receipts for lodging, travel tickets/receipts, and receipts for other
travel-related expenditures must be attached. The CCT-2 and attachments, must be
submitted to Human Resources for verification and certified by the employee’s
Department Head prior to the Mayor’s approval. After the Human Resources and Mayor’s
approval, the CCT-2 will be submitted to the City-Clerk-Treasurer’s Office for
reimbursement.

If there are any expenses for which a receipt cannot be provided, a Travel Attestation form
which can be provided by Human Resources needs to be filled out and submitted with the
Travel Reimbursement Form (CCT-2).

Any falsification or submittal for reimbursement for funds not spent will result in
disciplinary action, up to and including termination.

Mileage Allowance

Employees approved to utilize their personal vehicles on official City business/travel, will
be reimbursed for actual miles as well as tolls and parking fees. Under no circumstances
will fees for any kind of traffic/parking violation be reimbursed. Mileage, tolls, and
parking fees incurred in connection with an overnight trip will be reported on the Travel
Expense Report (CCT-2).

If an employee wishes to use a personal vehicle when a rental vehicle or City vehicle has
been deemed cheaper and more efficient, employees may do so but the City holds the right
to not reimburse mileage or to do so at a lower rate set by the Federal rate for these
situations. Also, employees attending college classes or study groups as a part of the
tuition reimbursement plan or on their own accord, will not be reimbursed for mileage.

Lodging

When possible, all lodging arrangements should be made and paid in advance by the City.
If lodging is to be paid using the City’s credit card, most hotels will require a Third-Party
Authorization/Credit Card Authorization form to be completed in advance of the check-
in date. This form must be requested from the hotel, completed by each department’s
designated employee in charge of travel arrangements, and faxed back to the hotel prior
to travel. Additional allowable charges paid by the employee will be reimbursed after
submission and approval of the request.

Meals/Per Diem

Travel requiring an overnight stay (as authorized by the employee’s supervisor) will be
authorized per diem up to the current Federal rate. For both the day travel begins and the
day travel ends, the per diem meal allowance is to be prorated by claiming ¾ of the per
diem meal allowance. If traveling to more than one location in one day, the per diem rate
for the area where stopping for rest or sleep will be used.

Transportation

When driving, employees may travel by City vehicle, personal vehicle, or rental car.
Whichever option is most affordable will be selected. Exceptions must be approved in
advance by the Human Resources Director. All rental cars will be booked in advance by
the Human Resources Department. Use of cabs, ride-shares, and shuttles are authorized
but receipts must be turned in for reimbursement. Any required air travel must be
arranged and paid for by the City prior to departure.

Travel Advance

The City is not authorized to pay travel advances.

No Show Charges

A full explanation for the cancellation should be attached to the expense report.

Elected Officials

The Mayor will be the approving authority for all budgeted travel by elected officials. Only
those expenditures relating to budgeted travel, as outlined above, are authorized and all
employee reimbursement rules apply.

 COMPENSATION

Workers’ Compensation

The City provides Workers’ Compensation (WC) coverage including medical and
indemnity benefits for loss of pay to employees who are injured on the job. Injuries
occurring while an employee is not performing employment services, including injuries
occurring while traveling to or from work or occurring away from the place of work during
unpaid lunch or break time are not covered. All compensation under this plan shall be in
accordance with applicable laws and policies.

Any employee injured on the job must contact his/her supervisor immediately regardless
of severity or if medical attention is required. Whether or not the employee is filing for
WC, each employee may be subject to a post-accident drug screening. The employee’s
supervisor will designate the appropriate place for the employee to submit to the drug
screening.

It is the supervisor’s responsibility to ensure all incident/accident reports are filed within
twenty-four (24) hours of the incident/accident. Department Heads and the Human
Resources Department are to be notified immediately of any such incident/accident.
Employees must use a facility designated as the WC provider by the City unless in
emergency situations in which employees must seek emergency treatment from a
hospital. The WC provider will also assist in referrals for secondary visits along with
secondary visits stemming from an emergency treatment at a hospital.

The City will supplement WC benefits for employees required by a physician to be off work
due to an occupational injury when light duty is not available for a maximum of ninety
(90) calendar days beginning from the date of injury/illness based on the WC claim.

The City will disperse this time by paying the full amount of the employee’s scheduled
hours for the first seven calendar days of the disability. If the employee’s disability lasts
longer than seven (7) calendar days, the City’s WC provider will pay the employee with
2/3 of the employee’s scheduled hours. The City will then pay 1/3 of the employee’s
scheduled hours up to the remaining eighty-three (83) calendar days. The payment
provided by WC and the City should be approximately equal to what an employee would
make if he or she was not on WC. The date(s) of payment from WC may not coincide with
the City’s normal payroll date.

After ninety (90) calendar days, the employee may supplement the WC with their own
sick, comp, or vacation time. The employee may only use one-third (1/3) of their
scheduled hours during this time. After ninety (90) calendar days of disability, the
employee will no longer accrue time off. Also, after these ninety (90) calendar days,
employees must enroll in FMLA and run it concurrently with the rest of any WC or paid
time off. For questions regarding FMLA please refer to the section titled Family Medical
Leave Act.

If an employee has no paid time off after the ninety (90) day period, he/she will go on
leave without pay. Employees are not allowed to draw sick time from the Catastrophic
Leave Program while on a WC injury. Once on LWOP status, the employee will be

 59

 COMPENSATION

responsible for paying their portion of all benefits that would have otherwise been
deducted from their pay. The employee is responsible for contacting the Human
Resources Department to obtain the amount of payment and when the payment will be
due each month.

After one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from the date of the WC claim, if the
employee can still not come back to work or light duty is not available, the Human
Resources Director, City Attorney, and Mayor will meet to determine the employee’s
employment status.

If an employee is approved for WC and the approved occupational injury or illness results
in termination of employment due to the employee’s inability to perform the essential
duties of their job and no other reasonable accommodation can be made; the employee
will be paid the full amount of sick leave permissible under normal retirement rules in
addition to all unused vacation, comp, or holiday pay.

While on WC, employees need to update their supervisor and the Human Resources
Department of any appointments and follow-up visits. Any doctor’s notes, return-to-work
orders, work-related restrictions, etc., need to be turned in immediately to the employee’s

While on WC, employees are not allowed to participate in any activity that is prohibited
by the attending physician. If an employee has a secondary job and the job does not
include any activity prohibited by the attending physician, he or she may continue this
job as long as work is not performed on a scheduled work day for the City. If it is
discovered the employee is violating this provision, the employee may receive disciplinary
action, up to and including termination.

Once an employee is released to return to duty, if the City has work-related concerns, the
City has the option to perform a return-to-duty exam utilizing a physician of the City’s
choosing at the expense of the City.

Once an employee is deemed fit to return to work from a WC injury, the City understands
that future doctor appointments or therapy may be necessary. While the City will allow
employees time off for these appointments, the employee will have to use his or her own
time or take leave without pay if no time is available. These appointments must be related
directly to the WC injury.

 LEAVE

Vacation Leave

All regular full-time employees who average at least thirty (30) work hours per week earn
vacation leave. Vacation leave must be earned before it is used and can be used in quarter-
hour increments. Employees may not borrow from future earnings or leave earned by
other employees. Employees continue to earn vacation leave at the normal accrual rate
when they are in pay status. Service is established on completed years and months of
service in a full-time, benefits-eligible position.

Vacation leave will be accrued on a bi-weekly basis. Employees accumulate leave but
cannot use leave for the first thirty (30) days of employment.

Vacation leave is usually approved for employees when it least interferes with the efficient
operation of your work unit and the City. To take vacation time, employees should try to
request advance approval from their supervisor. Requests will be reviewed based on
several factors, including deadlines, seniority, the order in which requests are submitted,
and staffing requirements. The City reserves the right to reschedule or deny vacation.
Vacation is paid at the employee’s base rate at the time vacation is taken. Vacation leave
counts as hours worked for the purposes of calculating overtime for all employees.

Upon separation from City employment, employees will be paid for unused vacation time
that has been earned through the last day of employment. Employees do not earn vacation
leave for the pay period when on leave without pay for more than three (3) shifts for non-
uniform employees, more than two (2) shifts for Police and Dispatch personnel, and more
than one (1) shift for Fire personnel. This excludes employees who choose to be on leave
without pay for military duty or those on military leave.

Sick Leave

All regular full-time employees that average at least thirty (30) work hours per week earn
sick leave. Sick leave must be earned before it is used and can be used in quarter-hour
increments. Employees may not borrow from future earnings or leave earned by other
employees. Employees continue to earn sick leave at the normal accrual rate when they
are in pay status.

Sick leave may be used due to the employee’s own illness or injury or to care for a spouse,
dependent 21 years of age or under, dependents older than 21 years of age who are
incapable of self-care because of a mental or physical disability, and parents. For the
purpose of this policy, this does not include parents-in-law.

Also, with the exception of a spouse, a dependent under the age of 21, or dependents older
than 21 years of age who are incapable of self-care because of a mental or physical
disability; an employee may not use sick leave to attend to a family member who has been
hospitalized. If additional leave is needed, employees should request leave under the
Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA). For more information on FMLA, please visit the
section titled Family Medical Leave.

Employees who are unable to report to work due to illness or injury will notify their direct
supervisor at least one (1) hour before the scheduled start of their workday unless they
are incapacitated. Department Heads or supervisors may require earlier notification in
order to ensure adequate staffing. Such a requirement must be provided to employees
prior to implementation.

Employees who are absent for three (3) or more consecutive days (two (2) or more
consecutive, regularly scheduled shifts for Fire department personnel working 48-hour
shifts) will be required to furnish a certificate of illness from an attending physician to the
Department Head or the Human Resources Director.

Employees using sick leave are not permitted to engage in outside employment. Also, once
an employee resigns from the City and gives a two-week notice, the employee will not be
allowed to use sick leave and the employee must use any remaining comp or vacation
leave if requesting time off. If no comp or vacation is available, the employee will have to
take leave without pay.

Sick leave does not count as hours worked for the purposes of calculating overtime.
Employees do not earn sick leave for the pay period when on leave without pay for more
than three (3) shifts for non-uniform employees, more than two (2) shifts for Police and
Dispatch personnel and more than one (1) shift for Fire personnel. This excludes
employees who choose to be on leave without pay for military duty or those on military
leave.

Leave Without Pay

An employee is placed on leave without pay (LWOP) status when he/she has exhausted
all accrued leave or if the employee is placed on leave without pay pending an
investigation. Employees shall not be granted LWOP for the purpose of other
employment. The only exception to this is employees on military duty.

Supervisors are responsible for monitoring leave balances. Supervisors should provide
guidance to employees with low balances and document such discussions with the
employee including attendance expectations.

With the exception of military employees who are on active duty or drill assignments and
employees who are on LWOP due to an FMLA or ADA event, LWOP must be requested in
writing or by email by the supervisor and may only be approved by the Human Resources
Director and Mayor. Failure to submit a request may result in disciplinary action for the
employee and his/her supervisor. Employees with disabilities covered by the Americans
with Disabilities Act may be entitled to LWOP as a reasonable accommodation.

Employees who fail to return to work on the date specified in the leave request without
receiving an extension in advance are subject to disciplinary action, up to and including
termination. The City may accept satisfactory reasons provided by the employee in
advance of the date to return to work and extend the leave period accordingly.

Leave Accrual While On LWOP

Employees do not earn sick or vacation accruals when on leave without pay for more than
three (3) shifts for non-uniform employees, more than two (2) shifts for Police and
Dispatch personnel and more than one (1) shift for Fire personnel per pay period. This
excludes employees who choose to be on leave without pay for military duty or those on
military leave.

Employees may choose to maintain health coverage and supplemental benefits while on
leave without pay. Employees who choose this option must pay the full cost of the
employee portion of the monthly premium. This includes employees on FMLA, ADA, or
military leave choosing to continue coverage. The payment should be mailed or delivered
to the Human Resources Director no later than the 1st day of the month by check or
money order payable to the City.

For extended periods of leave without pay, employees may be forced to enroll in COBRA
to maintain their health coverage. Employees on FMLA, ADA, or military leave are eligible
for reinstatement to the health coverage even if they opted to cancel while on leave. If an
employee has reason to believe he/she may be covered by FMLA, he/she should contact
the Human Resources Director as soon as possible.

Family and Medical Leave Act

The Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) requires public agencies to offer up to twelve
(12) weeks of job-protected unpaid leave a year to eligible employees for certain family
and medical reasons. For the purposes of this policy, a year is defined as twelve (12)
months beginning with the first day of approved FMLA.

Eligible City employees may take up to twelve (12) weeks of straight and in some cases
intermittent unpaid leave (accrued vacation, comp time, personal time, and sick leave
must be used prior to going on LWOP) for the following reasons:

 • The birth and care of the employee’s child, including bonding.
 • The placement of a child into an employee’s family by adoption or by foster-care
 arrangement and to care for the newly placed child.
 • The care of an immediate family member (spouse, child, or parent, but not a parent
 “in-law”) who has a serious health condition.
 • The employee’s own serious health condition.
 • For any qualifying exigency when the employee’s spouse, son, daughter, or parent
 is a covered military member (on active duty or is notified of an impending call to
 active duty) in support of a contingency operation.

Employees must conclude leave for the birth of a child or for adoption or foster care within
twelve (12) months after the event. However, leave may begin prior to birth or placement,
as circumstances dictate.

If spouses both work for the City and each wishes to take leave for the birth of a child,
adoption or placement of a child in foster care, or to care for a parent with a serious health
condition, the spouses may only take a combined total of twelve (12) weeks of leave. If
later during the year, either employee needs to take FMLA for another reason, he/she will
be eligible to use the remainder of time left up to twelve (12) weeks.

Eligible City employees may take up to twenty-six (26) weeks of unpaid leave (accrued
vacation, comp time, personal time and sick leave must be used prior to going on LWOP)
within a single twelve (12) month period for the care of a covered service member with a
serious injury or illness if the employee is the spouse, son, daughter, parent, or next of
kin.

If spouses both work for the City and each wishes to take leave to care for a covered injured
or ill service member, the spouses may only take a combined total of twenty-six (26) weeks
of leave. If an employee uses more than twelve (12) weeks for this instance, the employee
may not request additional time for an FMLA qualifying event.

FMLA leave is unpaid. However, employees must use any accrued paid leave during an
FMLA leave, and any available paid leave must be taken first. FMLA and other types of
leave (including workers’ compensation or disability leave) taken for the same reason run
concurrently.

An employee on leave as a result of a work-related injury that falls within the FMLA
definition of a serious health condition will be placed on FMLA leave if he or she cannot
return to work in 90 days. If an employee voluntarily elects to accept a light duty
assignment in lieu of FMLA leave, his or her right to be restored to the original or an
equivalent job and benefits continues until the end of the applicable FMLA leave year.
The employee should know that their pay on a light duty assignment may be lesser than
their normal pay.

FMLA Eligibility

To be eligible for the FMLA benefits employees must:

 • Be employed by the City for at least twelve (12) months, although the twelve (12)
 months of employment need not have been consecutive; and
 • Have physically worked one thousand two hundred fifty (1,250) hours over the
 previous twelve (12) months preceding the leave request. The twelve (12) months
 do not have to be consecutive.
 • An employee returning from fulfilling his or her National Guard or Reserve
 military obligation shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been
 performed but for the period of military service in determining whether the
 employee worked the 1,250 hours of service.

Calculation of Leave

There are four (4) permissible methods for calculating the 12-month period during which
the 12 weeks of FMLA leave may occur. The City has chosen the method in which
employees eligible for FMLA may use up to twelve (12) weeks of leave during a 12-month
period measured forward from the date the employee’s first date of FMLA leave begins.

For example, if an employee begins leave on September 1st, 2023, the employee will have
until August 31st, 2024, to use any eligible FMLA. Then on September 1st, 2024, the
employee is entitled to another twelve (12) weeks. If that same employee did not use
FMLA until October 1st, the FMLA calendar will then run from October 1st, 2024, until
September 30th, 2025.

Intermittent or Reduced Leave

In circumstances where FMLA leave is sought for your own serious health condition, or
that of a family member, you may take leave intermittently or be placed on a reduced work
schedule, if medically necessary. In addition, you may take leave intermittently or be
placed on a reduced work schedule for qualifying exigency and service member leave.

If you request intermittent or reduced leave status that is foreseeable based on planned
medical treatment, the City may in its sole discretion temporarily transfer you to another
job, with equivalent pay and benefits, if another position would better accommodate that
intermittent or reduced schedule. Furthermore, if the need to use intermittent or reduced

treatment, you should schedule the treatment in a manner that does not unduly disrupt
the City’s operations.

Requesting FMLA Leave

City employees are required to provide advance leave notice (at least 30 days) when leave
is foreseeable (such as childbirth, adoption, or planned medical treatment). If emergency
conditions prevent a thirty (30) day notification, employees must notify their supervisor
as soon as practicable.

It is the employee’s responsibility to request FMLA leave either verbally or in writing. The
process to request FMLA is detailed in the list below. While it is the employee’s
responsibility to request FMLA, the Human Resources Director will send all potentially
eligible employees notice of the right to use FMLA leave if they are absent for three (3) or
more consecutive days (three (3) or more consecutive, regularly scheduled shifts for Fire
department personnel working 48-hour shifts)

While the employee has the right to not request FMLA, the City holds the right to require
the employee to be on FMLA leave while the employee is absent from work for an
extended period of time due to the qualifying event. (In this type of event, the Human
Resources Director will notify the employee that the time off from work will be designated
as FMLA.) All FMLA paperwork will be sent by the Human Resources Department. There
will be four (4) worksheets included in this packet. Sections that are to be filled out, need
to be filled out completely.

 1. A Certification sheet for the health care provider. The type of certification will
 depend on the qualifying event.
 2. A Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (GINA) sheet. This will explain to
 the healthcare provider that the City does not require any family history of genetic
 information.
 3. An up-to-date job description for the health care provider to review. This will
 inform the health care provider what the essential duties and job functions the
 employee performs are.
 4. A Notice of Eligibility and Rights & Responsibilities. This informs the employee if
 they are eligible for leave and describes the above-mentioned paperwork that must
 be completed and returned.

Qualified health care providers include: doctors of medicine or osteopathy, podiatrists,
dentists, clinical psychologists, optometrists, chiropractors, nurse practitioners, nurse-
midwives, clinical social workers, and physician assistants authorized to practice under
State law and performing within the practice under State law.

Each employee has thirty (30) days to submit FMLA certification paperwork. This
includes the fifteen (15) day requirement to submit the paperwork and a fifteen (15) day
period to cure any vague, ambiguous, or non-responsive certifications. If complete and
responsive paperwork is not submitted within the thirty (30) day period, the leave may

receipt of the certification paperwork. In such cases, if the certification paperwork does
not substantiate the FMLA designation, the designation will be withdrawn and the
absence will be considered unexcused.

Upon submittal, each employee will receive a Designation Notice within three (3) days
notifying him or her of the approval or denial of FMLA status. If granted, it is the
employee’s responsibility to notify the Human Resources Department and the employee’s
supervisor every thirty (30) days of their ability to return to work. Before the employee
may return, they must be released by their doctor and have documentation.

If the City has reason to doubt the validity of a certification, the City may seek a second
opinion which will be paid by the City. If the second opinion differs from the first opinion,
then a third opinion will be sought. This will also be paid by the City and must be agreed
upon by the employee and the City. The result of the third opinion will be the opinion that
is accepted. In situations in which the serious health condition of the qualified member
lasts beyond a single leave year or is described as chronic, the City reserves the right to
require a new medical certification each following year. This will be at the employee’s
expense.

If an employee experiences more than one FMLA qualifying event at once, he/she will
have to submit FMLA paperwork for each event. There is no limit to how many FMLA
qualifying events may run concurrently at the same time. It is the employee’s
responsibility to inform the Human Resources Department or the supervisor which event
the leave is for if the employee needs to be absent.

Release to Return to Work

Upon return to work, as requested in the original paperwork, the employee must be able

Leave Program, the employee may be eligible for additional leave through that program,
but this is not guaranteed. For more information on the Catastrophic Sick Leave Program,
please review the section titled Catastrophic Sick Leave Program.

Employee Rights Under FMLA

The City will maintain the employee’s health coverage under any group plan during the
time the employee is on FMLA leave under the same conditions as if the employee
continued to work. Arrangements will need to be made for employees to pay their share
of health insurance premiums while on unpaid leave at any time during the twelve (12)
weeks. If the premium is not paid within thirty (30) days, the employee will be sent notice

City will grant a reasonable amount of paid time off to vote. The City reserves the right to
select the hours employees are excused to vote and Department Heads or supervisors
must be notified of the need to leave due to voting as soon as possible.

While on voting leave, employees are to do nothing else other than vote, unless pre-
approved by the supervisor or Department Head. Failure to comply with this may result
in disciplinary action.

The City also reserves the right to deny the time off to vote if an employee can still vote
after his/her scheduled hours.

 78

 LEAVE

Jury Duty / Court Leave

Full-time employees will be granted leave with pay for jury duty or if they are subpoenaed
as a witness during scheduled work hours. Employees are also permitted to retain the
allowance for services from the court for such service.

To qualify for jury or witness duty leave, employees must submit to his/her supervisor a
copy of the summons upon receipt. Proof of services must be submitted to the supervisor
when jury or witness duty is completed. If the employee is excused from jury duty early
or not required to be present in court, he/she is expected to report to work. Failure to
comply with this may result in disciplinary action. Jury or witness duty time will be coded
in the time system as jury duty. This leave will be paid at the employee’s current rate of
pay and will be considered time worked for overtime purposes.

All employees subpoenaed as a part of their duties as a City of Cabot employee, will need
to record the hours on his or her timecard as hours worked and will also be permitted to
retain the allowance for services from the court for that such service.

This policy of paid leave does not apply to employees who initiate court proceedings on
their own behalf.

 79

 LEAVE

Inclement Weather Leave

The City will maintain critical operations, even during inclement weather. While some
services of the City may not be provided due to the weather conditions, those employees
who are designated to work will be required to work at no additional pay. These include
or may include, Police, Fire, Animal Services, and Street department employees.
Additional departments or employees may be designated to work during inclement
weather conditions.

The Mayor or his/her designee will determine if the City will be closed for inclement
weather. Employees, supervisors, and Department Heads will be notified. If any employee
has any questions if he/she is required to be at work, the employee should contact the
supervisor or Department Head.

If inclement weather conditions begin during the workday, the Mayor or his/her designee
will make a determination concerning any early closing of City Departments. If an
employee wishes to leave during inclement weather, the Department Head may permit
those employees to use vacation, comp or personal leave to be excused from duty.

If inclement weather is in effect and the City does not close, employees are expected to
report at normal time if they are able to safely travel to their worksite. If an employee is
not able to travel to work as a result of road conditions, employees are expected to contact
their supervisor or Department Head immediately. In the event an employee cannot make
it to work, the employee may have to use vacation or compensatory leave. This will vary
from Department to Department. Employees may not use sick leave.

During inclement weather closures, employees designated to work, such as Police, Fire,
or Street employees, must report to work. If a designated employee is having difficulty
making it to work, the employee must notify his/her supervisor immediately. Designated
employees who fail to show up during inclement weather may be subject to disciplinary
action, up to termination.

Any employee who has PTO scheduled and the City closes his or her department for
inclement weather, will have that scheduled leave reimbursed.

 80

 LEAVE

Catastrophic Sick Leave Program

The Catastrophic Sick Leave Bank Program provides paid leave to City employees when
the employee or an immediate family member requiring their care faces a catastrophic
illness or injury and the employee would otherwise go on leave without pay. (This does
not include pregnancy.) Employees enroll in the Catastrophic Sick Leave Program
voluntarily by donating earned sick leave to a pool of leave for use by other eligible
employees.

Regular full-time City employees must meet the following minimum requirements to be
eligible for Catastrophic Leave:

 • Provide a certification from a physician documenting a medical condition
 requiring leave for a prolonged period of time for the employee or employee’s
 immediate family member (spouse, parent, or child).
 • Participate in the catastrophic leave bank program including enrollment and the
 minimum contribution of eight (8) hours to join and four (4) hours annually.
 • A minimum of one year of service as a full-time employee.
 • Already submitted all FMLA or other applicable paperwork to cover the employee’s
 extended leave of absence.
 • A minimum accrual of 80 hours (vacation and sick combined) at the beginning of
 the illness.
 • Employees must be, or reasonably expected to be, on leave without pay status.
 • A letter must be provided from the employee’s Department Head regarding any
 history of leave abuse.
 • Employees must be enrolled for six months prior to eligibility.

The Human Resources Department holds the responsibility to maintain the balance of
the Catastrophic Leave pool and report it to the Catastrophic Leave Committee as
requested. Employees may not receive leave from the Catastrophic Leave Bank while on
a WC injury.

Catastrophic Leave Committee

A committee made up of four (4) participants in the Catastrophic Leave Bank Program
will be appointed by the Human Resource Director to review all requests and determine
whether to grant Catastrophic Leave. If one of the four (4) participants cannot make the
meeting, the Human Resources Director will appoint another member of the program for
that particular request. The City Attorney will also serve as a voting member of the
Catastrophic Leave Committee. The Human Resource Director will not vote on any
decision. Leave granted may not exceed the latter of:

 • The date the employee or family member is released to duty (full or modified) by
 the treating physician; or

 81

 LEAVE

 • The date of eligibility for disability benefits. Catastrophic leave cannot be awarded
 retroactively. The maximum award permitted is six (6) months in any two (2) year
 period beginning from the initial use of catastrophic leave.

Applications for Catastrophic Leave will be reviewed on a first-filed, first-considered
basis. Catastrophic Leave, which would result in a negative balance of the City’s
Catastrophic Leave Bank, will not be approved.

Donations to the Catastrophic Sick Leave Program

Upon enrollment, employees will contribute eight (8) hours of sick leave to join the
program. After enrollment, an annual four (4)-hour contribution will be automatically
deducted from accrued sick leave at the end of each December. Employees may only
donate four (4) sick hours each December. Employees may NOT donate vacation leave at
any point nor may employees donate any time that will be forfeited at the end of the year
due to maximum carryover rules.

Employees will not be required to make an annual donation for up to six (6) months after
their illness or injury. Donations to the Catastrophic Leave Program are not tax
deductible. Participation will continue until the participating employee requests
termination of participation in writing. Enrollment and Catastrophic Leave Request
forms are available from the Human Resources Department.

In the event that for any reason an employee who is a member of the Catastrophic Sick
Leave Program is terminated, resigns, or leaves the City for any reason, he/she may not
donate remaining sick or any type of leave to the program.

Requesting Catastrophic Leave

A participating employee who has exhausted all available leave time and who presents
documentation of the ongoing illness from the treating physician may request leave time
from the Catastrophic Leave Program. Employees or their designees must file the
following documents: Recipient Application and Physicians Certification.

Forms should be presented to the Human Resources Director in time for review and
consideration before an employee goes on leave without pay. Catastrophic Leave Forms
are available from the Human Resources Department. Any unused Catastrophic Leave
will be returned to the program in the event the employee is terminated, retires, or returns
to work prior to the expiration of the previously approved Catastrophic Leave Period.

 82

 LEAVE

Funeral / Bereavement Leave

Full-time employees may be granted pay up to a maximum of three (3) calendar days (two
scheduled shifts for Fire department employees on a 48-hour schedule) of absence with
pay due to the death of a member of the employees’ or spouses’ immediate family.

The immediate family for the purposes of this policy will include the spouse, parents,
siblings, children, grandparents, grandchildren, and guardian or any of the spouse’s
family members listed above. Any exceptions to this policy will be made only at the
discretion of the Mayor. Funeral or Bereavement Leave will count as hours worked
towards overtime. This will be coded in the time system as bereavement leave.

Travel time of one (1) day may be granted upon prior approval of the Department Head
and the Human Resources Director.

Pets

The City understands the bond between an animal and a family. Therefore, the City will
grant one (1) paid day of leave under the bereavement policy if an employee’s dog or cat
dies during an employee’s shift or before an employee is scheduled to go on shift. This
paid day of leave must be approved by the Department Head and the Human Resources
Director. This type of leave can be awarded retroactively as well.

An employee wanting to take off work to care for a sick or injured animal may do so at the
supervisor’s discretion and must use vacation, comp, or personal time.

 83

 BENEFITS

Health Insurance

The City of Cabot offers group health insurance coverage to all full-time employees. Full-
time employees are designated as averaging thirty (30) or more hours per week. The
employee is eligible for health insurance on the first day of the month following two
complete full months of employment.

For example, if an employee started work on January 1st, he/she would work the complete
month of January and February and be eligible on March 1st. If an employee started
January 15th, the month of January would not count towards eligibility as the employee
would not have worked the full month. Therefore, the employee would be eligible for
health insurance on April 1st.

The City currently pays an employer percentage of the premium for individual and family
coverage and the employee pays the remaining percentage. The City reserves the right to
change insurance providers or premium percentages.

Tri-Care Insurance
As allowed by law, the City will pay the premium for Tri-Care health insurance for all full-
time employees who are active guard or reserve military members. This amount will not
exceed the amount the City pays for the lowest single and family coverage on the City-
provided group insurance plan.

Those enrolled in the program will have to fill out the necessary paperwork including
submitting proof of payment each month to the Human Resources Office. After the
employee submits proof of payment, the City will process a payment to the employee.

Failure to submit proof or provide the necessary information may result in the premium
not being paid or delayed.

High-Deductible Health Plan
If the City provides a high-deductible health plan, the City will contribute to the
employee’s Health Savings Account (HSA) quarterly at a designated amount as
determined each year by the Mayor and Human Resources Director.

Those hired before 12/31/2022 and who were already enrolled in the City’s co-pay health
insurance plan have the option of the City’s co-pay or high-deductible plan each year at
open enrollment.

 84

 BENEFITS

Supplemental Insurance

The City of Cabot offers supplemental insurance coverage to all full-time employees. Full-
time employees are designated as averaging thirty (30) or more hours per week. The
employee is eligible for supplemental coverage on the first of the month following one
complete month of employment.

For example, if an employee started work on January 1st, he/she would work the complete
month of January and be eligible on February 1st. If an employee started January 15th,
the month of January would not count towards eligibility as the employee would not have
worked the full month. Therefore, the employee would be eligible for health insurance on
March 1st.

The City currently pays seventy-five percent (75%) of elected coverage for Delta Dental
and Vision Choice Plans (VSP) and the employee pays twenty-five percent (25%). The City
reserves the right to change insurance providers or premium percentages.

The City also provides a term life insurance policy to all full-time employees.

Finally, the City currently offers other vendors providing a variety of plans including, but
not limited to: life insurance, disability, critical illness, cancer, flex-spending, accident,
and other policies. The employee will pay the full premium for these additional
supplemental policies.

 85

 BENEFITS

Open Enrollment

Each year in the 4th quarter, the City will offer all full-time employees an open enrollment
period. During this time, each employee will have an opportunity to add, drop, or change
benefit coverage. If an employee fails to do so during this time period, the employee may
not be able to add, drop, or change certain coverage until the next open enrollment.

Employees will be given ample notice for open enrollment and attendance will be
mandatory unless excused by the Human Resources Director.

 86

 BENEFITS

Employee Assistance Program

The City offers employees an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) at no charge to all
employees.

The EAP offers counseling services to employees, their families, or anyone living in the
residence at no cost. EAP will assist employees with a variety of concerns including but
not limited to anxiety, depression, death, divorce, money, substance abuse, etc. EAP is
strictly confidential and the City will have no records of an employee’s voluntary visit to
an EAP site.

As part of the City’s responsibility to make sure employees receive the proper training or
counseling they need, the City reserves the right to mandate employees to attend an EAP
session to review matters such as anger, discipline, or other areas of concern. Mandates
will be determined at the discretion of the Mayor, Department Head, and the Human
Resource Director. Any failure to attend or comply with an EAP mandate will result in
disciplinary action, up to and including termination. All mandated EAP sessions will be
compensated.

EAP Visit During Scheduled Work Hours

Due to the increase in mental health issues, each calendar year the City will provide each
employee one (1) opportunity to visit with an EAP location during their normally
scheduled work hours. The City realizes that in situations of abuse, depression, or other
issues, employees might never utilize this benefit if not allowed this opportunity.

The employee should let his or her supervisor and the Human Resources Department
know this benefit is being used. While there is no time limit on this visit, the employee
must attend the session and not use the time for personal matters unconnected to the EAP
visit. Violation of this policy could result in disciplinary action.

 87

 BENEFITS

Educational Assistance Program

The City recognizes that the skills and knowledge of its employees are critical to the
success of the organization. The Education Assistance Program is for employees seeking
undergraduate or graduate coursework from fully accredited institutions. The program
encourages personal development through formal education so that employees can
maintain and improve job-related skills or enhance their ability to compete for reasonably
attainable jobs with the City.

Within the yearly budget, tuition assistance will be provided for graduate and post-
graduate coursework, excluding doctorate programs. The City will not pay for more than
three (3) credit hours per term, up to twelve (12) credit hours per calendar year. The City
has requirements for the Education Assistance Program that must ALL be met before an
employee can participate.

 • A continuous full-time active employee of the City for a minimum of one (1) year.
 • Completion of the Tuition Assistance Request application form (TAR-1) prior to
 attending the course.
 • Participation shall be restricted to off-duty hours and is not to interfere with the
 normal performance of the employee’s duties; if the employee is caught working
 on assignments or doing homework during work hours, he/she may be disciplined.
 (This does not apply to fire employees working 48-hour shifts, but must be done
 during designated free time).
 • Courses shall be limited to those that lead to improvement in job performance and
 apply to degree requirements related to the employee’s current job duties or a
 foreseeable future position. Course enrollment shall be limited to accredited
 institutions only.
 • Reimbursement will be based on successful completion of coursework with a grade
 of “C” or higher. Any grades of “D” or “F”, Withdrawals, or Incompletes will not be
 reimbursed.
 • Expenses paid by the City shall include tuition plus other standard enrollment fees
 (online fees, registration fees, books, technology fees, etc.). Specialized / Non-
 Traditional fees that will not be paid by the City include but are not limited to
 equipment rental, purchase or use fees, travel or transportation fees, late
 enrollment fees, etc.
 • Reimbursement by the City will be made when the participant completes the
 Tuition Assistance Reimbursement form (TAR-2).

The City’s tuition reimbursement program meets the requirements listed in the IRS Code
for an Education Assistance Program. Employees eligible for other financial aid
(scholarships, grants, etc.) will only be reimbursed for the difference between the amount
received from the other funding source and the actual cost. While educational assistance
is expected to enhance employee’s performance and professional abilities, the City cannot
guarantee that participation in formal education will entitle the employee to automatic
advancement, a different job assignment, or pay increases. The projected assistance
expense to the City must be within approved budget limitations.

 88

 BENEFITS

Retirement

Non-Uniformed Employees including Dispatch

All full-time, non-uniformed employees, including Dispatch employees, shall participate
in the Arkansas Public Employees Retirement System (APERS). This also includes regular
part-time employees who at any point in employment have three (3) consecutive months
of at least eighty (80) hours worked. Employees and the City shall contribute at the rate
designated by APERS. For additional information regarding the retirement system,
employees are encouraged to read the APERS retirement booklet, go online to the APERS
website, or contact the Human Resources Department.

Police and Fire Employees

All uniformed full-time employees shall participate in the Arkansas Local Police and Fire
Retirement System (LOPFI). Police employees shall contribute at the rate designated by
LOPFI and pay into Social Security. Fire employees shall contribute at the rate designated
by and not pay into Social Security. All Fire employees will receive a notice upon
employment, concerning Social Security. The City shall contribute at the rate designated
by LOPFI. For additional information regarding the retirement system, employees are
encouraged to read the LOPFI retirement booklet, go online to the LOPFI website, or
contact the Human Resources Department.

Volunteer/Part-Time Fire Employees

All volunteer Fire Department employees will be given a LOPFI retirement credit.
Members will not contribute to the plan. The contribution amount for the City and the
qualifying status as volunteer or full-time employment for employees will be determined
by LOPFI yearly.

 89

 BENEFITS

Retiree Health Benefits

The City offers extended coverage to retired employees and their families after their
employment with the City as allowed by the City’s Health, Dental, and Vision providers.
Retirees electing to extend coverage after employment may do so if they meet all of the
following requirements:

 • Employee must be age fifty-five (55) or over;
 • Employee must complete twenty (20) years of service to the City of Cabot;
 • Employee must be receiving a retirement benefit from the Arkansas Local Police
 and Fire Retirement System, Arkansas Public Employees Retirement System, or a
 local pension fund.

Any employee who completes twenty-eight (28) years of service to the City of Cabot and
is receiving a retirement benefit from APERS or LOPFI is also eligible regardless of age.

If the employee meets all of these criteria, he/she may continue coverage after retirement.
The retiree must pay the entire portion of the premium. The retiree must also have the
premium to the City Clerk/Treasurer’s Office no later than the end of business on the 5th
day of the month. Failure to pay the entire premium on or before the 5th will result in the
retiree being terminated from the plan.

Any employee who is terminated from the City of Cabot will not be eligible for retiree
health benefits.

Employees are eligible for retiree coverage on the City’s sponsored health insurance,
dental insurance, and vision insurance plans.

If a retiree elects to continue a City-sponsored high-deductible health plan, the City will
continue to contribute to the retiree’s HSA at the same amount and distribution dates that
the City contributes to active employee HSAs. To be eligible for the HSA plan or this
contribution benefit from the City post-retirement, the retiree and no dependents can be
on Medicare at any point.

 90

 BENEFITS

Line of Duty Death

For all full-time employees employed by the City and enrolled in the City’s primary health
insurance plan, if an employee dies in the line of duty, the City will pay the employee and
the employer’s portion of the health insurance premiums for up to 3 years for all eligible
dependents who are covered under the plan as dependents at the time the employee is
killed in the line of duty as allowed by the Health provider’s plan. This does not apply to
“extra” or “supplemental” policies.

Line of duty death will be defined as:

 • Injuries resulting in death that occur while the employee is being paid for time
 worked and the employee is acting in the capacity of a City employee and
 performing official job duties that he or she would normally or reasonably perform.

Exclusion to this policy will happen when death occurs as a result of:

 • While the employee is going to or from work and the event that causes death has
 nothing to do with the employee’s job or job tasks.
 • Self-inflicted injuries or intentional injuries that lead to death.
 • Any alcohol or non-prescribed drug-related incident.
 • A result of natural causes including heart attack, stroke, or disease, including if a
 natural cause occurs while an employee is performing his or her normal job duties
 or tasks.
 • As a result of injuries received more than one year before the date of the employee’s
 death unless, before the expiration of five years from the date of the injury, the
 dependents provide medical proof acceptable to the City that death was due to an
 injury that occurred in the line of duty.

As stated, eligible dependents will be able to receive the insurance completely paid by the
City for up to 3 years. The following will result in the City no longer paying the full
premium prior to the end of 3 years:

 • The dependents enroll in another group policy or plan. Once the dependents leave
 the City’s plan, they are not allowed to return to the plan.
 • If a child dependent reaches the limiting age as stated in the plan.
 • If the City no longer provides health insurance to employees. (This does not include
 if the City switches providers which the City reserves the right to do)

At any point the dependents come off of the insurance for any of the reasons listed above
or 3 years pass, the dependents will be sent a COBRA notice and if eligible, they can
continue to pay the full premium for a specified amount of time.

If the health plan is a City-sponsored high deductible plan, the City will continue to
contribute to the deceased employee’s HSA at the same amount and distribution dates
that the City contributes to active employee HSAs.

 91

‭ urpose:‬‭To provide a comprehensive infection control‬‭system that maximizes protection‬

‭ cope: This policy applies to all CFD members, career and part-time, providing rescue or‬

‭ abot Fire Department recognizes that communicable disease exposure is an occupational health‬
C
‭hazard. Communicable disease transmission is possible during any aspect of emergency‬
 ‭response, including in-station operations. The health and welfare of each member is a joint‬
 ‭concern of the member, the officers and this department. While each member is ultimately‬
 ‭responsible for his or her own health, the department recognizes a responsibility to provide as‬
 ‭safe a workplace as possible. The goal of this program is to provide all members with guidance‬

‭It is the policy of CFD:‬

‭ o provide rescue and emergency medical services to the public without regard to known or‬

‭suspected diagnosis of communicable disease in any patient.‬

‭ o regard all patient contacts as potentially infectious. Standard precautions will be observed at‬
T
‭all times and will be expanded to include all body fluids and other potentially infectious material.‬

‭ o provide all members with the necessary training, immunizations, and personal protective‬
T
‭equipment (PPE) needed for protection from communicable diseases.‬

‭To recognize the need for work restrictions based on infection control concerns.‬

‭ o prohibit discrimination of any member for health reasons, including infection and/or‬
T
‭seroconversion with HIV/HBV virus.‬

‭ o regard all medical information as strictly confidential. No member’s health information will‬
T
‭be released without written consent of the member/patient.‬

The purpose of this agreement is to establish a combined communications
network, which shall be known as the Lonoke County Emergency Communications
Center (“911 Center”), to better provide for the health, safety, and welfare of all
citizens of Lonoke County. The 911 Center shall be located within the municipal
boundaries of Cabot.

The further purpose is to streamline the dispatching of non-emergency and
emergency calls as received over the 911 telephone system and by other means.

The location of the Public Safety Answering Point (“PSAP”) shall be determined by
the Lonoke County 911 Governing Board.

The combined PSAP will serve the areas of, but not be limited to, the
unincorporated areas of Lonoke County, Arkansas, and the incorporated areas of
Allport, Austin, Cabot, Coy, England, Humnoke, Keo, Lonoke, and Ward.

SECTION 5: MANNER OF FINANCING

The City of Cabot will have full responsibility for management of the finances to
operate the Center along with Human Resources functions (pay and benefits).

City of Cabot budget process and the 911 Governing Board.
All procurement for the 911 Center, 911 System and associated equipment, shall
be governed by the City of Cabot purchasing and procurement procedures.

or allocated by the Arkansas 911 Board to any governmental entity within Lonoke
County, shall go to the operating expenses of the 911 Center.
Should there be a shortfall in operating funds, the following governmental entities
will contribute to the shortfall based upon the percentage of their population

the proposed date of withdrawal.

ORDINANCE NO. 34 OF 2023

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND SECTION 2-579 OF THE CODE OF CABOT;
DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the contract change order provisions of Section 2-579 of the Code of Cabot
have not been amended in approximately twenty years and do not reflect the ways that Cabot has
grown in the intervening time nor the scope of projects that are now being undertaken to further
improve the community; and

WHEREAS, the City desires that the Code be amended to reflect current development
conditions, while still maintaining strong oversight by the City Council.

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council therefore wishes to amend Section 2-579 consistent
with the attached Exhibit A.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: Code of Cabot Sec. 2-579 is hereby amended consistent with the attached
Exhibit A, which is incorporated herein by this reference.

SECTION 2: Any municipal legislation or portion of municipal legislation in conflict
with this Ordinance is hereby repealed to the extent of the conflict.

SECTION 3: If any provision of this Ordinance or the application thereof is held invalid,
such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of the Ordinance which can be
given effect without the invalid provisions or application, and to this end, the provisions of this
Ordinance are declared to be severable.

SECTION 4: The City of Cabot has multiple on-going projects, including infrastructure
improvements and others that directly benefit the health, safety, and welfare of the citizens of
Cabot. An emergency is therefore declared so that those projects may move forward without any
unnecessary delays and so that the benefits of those projects may more quickly accrue to the
residents of Cabot. As such, the provisions of this Ordinance shall take effect immediately upon
its passage.

Holiday and Holiday Pay

Non-Uniformed Employees

The City will grant paid time off to all full-time employees on the holidays listed below:

 x New Year’s Day January 1st
 x Martin Luther King Day Third Monday in January
 x Presidents’ Day Third Monday in February
 x Good Friday Friday preceding Easter
 x Memorial Day Last Monday in May
 x Juneteenth June 19th
 x Independence Day July 4th
 x Labor Day First Monday in September
 x Columbus Day Second Monday in October (effective 2024)
 x Veteran’s Day November 11th
 x Thanksgiving Day Fourth Thursday in November
 x Day After Thanksgiving Fourth Friday in November
 x Christmas Eve December 24th
 x Christmas Day December 25th
 x New Year’s Eve December 31st
 x Personal Day Anniversary Date (1st day of the month following one
 year of employment)

The Mayor may issue an order granting additional days as holidays in observance of
special events or for other reasons.

Non-Uniformed Employees

A recognized holiday that falls on a Saturday will be observed on the preceding Friday. A
recognized holiday that falls on a Sunday will be observed on the following Monday. If a
holiday occurs during an eligible employee’s paid absence (such as vacation or sick leave),
holiday pay will be provided instead of the paid time off. Employees on leave without pay
status will not be compensated for holiday pay. Employees working on a holiday will
receive pay for the number of hours worked at the appropriate rate in addition to the eight
(8) hours of holiday pay. Employees on FMLA paid leave status will be compensated for
holiday pay. Holiday pay will be counted as hours worked for the purposes of determining
overtime.

Each full-time employee will also receive a personal day after one (1) year of employment
and an additional personal day each year of employment the month of the employee’s
anniversary day. Personal Days must be taken in eight (8) hour increments. Employees
who have over eight (8) hours of personal time, must take this time before using vacation
days. Personal days will be counted as hours worked for the purposes of determining
overtime.

10/26/2023

Chad Moreau

3064 Mtn Springs Rd

Cabot, AR 72023

To Whom It May Concern,

 My name is Chad Moreau and I am writing today to express my interest in joining the Cabot
Parks and Rec Commission Board. My wife, Natasha and three children, Mitchell, Camden and Savannah,
have lived in Cabot for the past 11 years. We have been active in Cabot parks and rec throughout the
years. From baseball to cheer to basketball, we coach, taxi and cheer our kids on every step of the way! I
have served as head coach/assistant coach in some capacity for the past 7+ years. I enjoy being able to
teach kids the proper way to play a sport, to be a great teammate and to give 110% in everything they
do.

 I own a medical supply company in Conway, AR called Baker Medical, Inc. We provide
CPAP/BiPap equipment and supplies to patients throughout the state of Arkansas. My wife and I also
own a commercial real estate company called Moreau Properties of Arkansas, LLC. We are active
members of Faith Missionary Baptist Church in Cabot. We love our church and have been serving there
for over 10 years. We thoroughly enjoy Wednesday night Awana because we can work with children
every week encouraging and mentoring them.

 I currently serve on the Cabot Parks and Rec Discipline Oversight Committee. I strive to be a
voice of reason while serving, but also pride myself on making sure rules are followed and children are
protected. I love seeing my children excel in their activities. Seeing them grow throughout the year,
persevere through defeat and accomplish a goal is what it’s all about. I believe a good coach must be
able to effectively communicate with their players, providing a clear understanding of expectations,
consequences and team goals. Furthermore, the coach must be able to resolve conflicts on and off the
field because conflicts are bound to happen in kid sports. Whether a bad call is made, or a parent is
disgruntled, the coach must be a steady anchor, someone the players can rely on when times get tough.

 If chosen, my plan is to serve this board and community with everything I have. I know my
experience will allow me to provide helpful insight into all points of discussion. Again, I enjoy serving and
I feel this board allows me to do just that. Please let me know if you have any questions or concerns
regarding my request and I will be happy to answer them.

Thank you for the opportunity.

Cordially,

Chad Moreau, MBA

ORDINANCE NO. 35 OF 2023

AN ORDINANCE ACKNOWLEDGING THAT A CITY OFFICIAL PLANS TO
DO BUSINESS WITH THE CABOT PARKS AND RECREATION
COMMISSION, SPECIFICALLY STEPHEN REDD AND HIS COMPANY;
PERMITTING SAID BUSINESS TO THE EXTENT NECESSARY; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, Stephen Redd, through his company Arkansas Yeehaw Pyrotechnic
Productions, provided firework services to the Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission
for the Commission’s 2023 fourth of July celebration. Said services were authorized
under Ordinance 12 of 2023. Stephen Redd and his company have been selected by the
Commission to provide firework services for a further three years; and

WHEREAS, The Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission (the Commission) is,
under both state law and city ordinance, an independent commission with independent
control over its own financial affairs. The Commission, duly following its own rules and
procedures on financial expenditures and the procurement of services, selected Redd to
provide the above-mentioned services; and

WHEREAS, this Ordinance is being promulgated in the interest of transparency
of the actions of City officials. The Cabot City Council herein finds that the offering of
services discussed herein does not implicate A.C.A. 14-42-107 as the services are being
provided to an independent commission with independent control over its own financial
affairs and service procurement under A.C.A. 14-269-202 et seq. Neither the Cabot City
Council nor the City of Cabot exercise any control nor authority over the day-to-day
affairs and expenditures of the Commission. As such, the Cabot City Council finds that a
conflict with the City does not exist through the offering of services and conducting of
business discussed herein. However, to the extent it may later be deemed necessary, the
offering of services and conducting of business discussed herein is permitted to the extent
such permit is necessary.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The Cabot City Council herein acknowledges that Stephen Redd
and his above referenced business plan on conducting business with the Cabot Parks and
Recreation Commission, an independent commission established under A.C.A. 14-269-
202 et seq, to provide firework services to the Commission for a period of three years. To
the extent this governing’s body’s permission is necessary for the conducting of said

business, it is hereby granted.

RESOLUTION NO. 70 OF 2023

A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND CITY CLERK-
TREASURER TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH BARGER
EXCAVATING, INC TO PROVIDE EXTERIOR SITE WORK FOR
THE CABOT JUSTICE CENTER PROJECT; TO WAIVE THE
COMPETITIVE BIDDING REQUIREMENTS IN ORDER TO ENTER
INTO SAID AGREEMENT; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, pursuant to Ordinance 12 of 2021 a special election was conducted in August
of 2021 on the issuance of Sale and Use Tax Refunding and Improvement Bonds. Among the
projects authorized by the results of the special election were police department facility construction
and improvements and drainage improvements; and

WHEREAS, in Ordinance 4 of 2023, the City Council Authorized the issuance of Franchise
Fee Revenue Bonds, Series 2023. Per that ordinance, the revenue raised by said bonds would be
used for courts and police facilities; and

WHEREAS, in Resolution 17 of 2023, the Cabot City Council authorized the City to
begin preliminary design work for the Cabot Justice Center in order to accomplish the
construction and improvements of the police department facilities as referenced in the above
two paragraphs; and

WHEREAS, in Resolution 33 of 2023, the Cabot City Council, after having completed
the legal requirements for the procurement of professional services, authorized the City to
negotiate with Baldwin & Shell to provide construction management services for the Cabot
Justice Center Project; and

WHEREAS, the City has completed negotiations with Baldwin & Shell as authorized
in Resolution 33 of 2023. As part of that process, Baldwin & Shell conducted biddings for
multiple sections of the overall project. One of those sections was exterior site work and Barger
Excavating, Inc (Barger) returned the lowest bid for said work.

WHEREAS, A.C.A. 14-58-303 provides that the governing body may waive the
requirement of competitive bidding in situations where the procedure is deemed not feasible or
practical. In this case, internal bidding had already been done by Baldwin & Shell and the lowest
bidder for the required work has already been identified. It would be an unnecessary use of
public funds and a delay in the project to conduct further bidding only to reach the same result.
The Cabot City Council therefore finds that the requirement of competitive bidding in this
matter is neither feasible nor practical and is hereby waived; and

WHEREAS, the City Council acknowledges that the overall Cabot Justice Center
Project will be paid for with funds, where applicable, from: the Franchise Fee Revenue Bonds
authorized by Resolution 4 of 2023; the relevant bonds of the Sale and Use Tax Refunding
Bonds authorized by Ordinance 12 of 2021 and the subsequent special election; the Sidewalk
Fund; and the General Fund.
